title: Smooth Proper Curves Divisors Genus and Ramification

items.title: Curves over a field
items.statement: Let k be a field. A curve over k is a k-scheme that is geometrically integral, separated and of finite type, and whose underlying topological space has chain dimension one. A smooth curve (resp. proper curve) is a curve whose structure morphism to Spec k is smooth (resp. proper); smoothness and properness are extra adjectives, never part of the word curve.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21
William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy), Chs. 6-8

items.title: Normalization of an integral finite-type curve by gluing affine integral closures
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. It is inherited through the normality-locality criterion and the finite-morphism criteria for finiteness and integrality used in the proof. Let $C$ be an integral separated finite-type curve over a field $k$ with function field $K=k(C)$, and let $C=U_1\cup\cdots\cup U_n$ be a finite affine cover with $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}(A_i)$. The integral closures $B_i$ of $A_i$ in $K$ are finite $A_i$-modules and their formation commutes with principal localisation. On each overlap $U_i\cap U_j$, common principal-open refinements give identifications of the corresponding localizations inside $K$, so the $\operatorname{Spec}(B_i)$ glue over the overlaps to a scheme $C^{\mathrm{nu}}$ and a morphism $
u:C^{\mathrm{nu}}	o C$. Then $C^{\mathrm{nu}}$ is integral and normal, $
u$ is finite, affine and birational, $k(C^{\mathrm{nu}})=K$, and $(C^{\mathrm{nu}},
u)$ is the normalization of $C$: it is initial among normal integral schemes finite and birational over $C$, hence unique up to unique isomorphism over $C$.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy), Chs. 6-8
Jiahui Gao and Shouwu Zhang, Lectures on Algebraic Geometry (December 14, 2019), Ch. 7

items.strategy: Prove each affine closure finite and normal, identify overlaps by localizations in K, glue, and verify finiteness, birationality, and chartwise initiality.

items.title: Rational maps of integral finite-type schemes
items.statement: Let X and Y be integral k-schemes of finite type with Y separated over k. A rational map phi:X⇢Y is an equivalence class of pairs (U,phi_U) consisting of a nonempty open subscheme U of X and a k-morphism phi_U:U→Y, where two pairs are equivalent when their morphisms agree on a nonempty open subscheme of the intersection of their domains; this relation is an equivalence relation, transitivity following from the agreement criterion on a dense open subscheme of a reduced source with separated target. A rational map is dominant when some representative is dominant, that is, has dense image. A point of X at which no representative is defined is a point of indeterminacy of the rational map.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21

items.title: Rational maps from a smooth curve to a proper scheme are morphisms
items.statement: Assume Choice through the stated curve, DVR, valuative and separated-target criteria. Every rational map from a smooth curve X over k to a proper k-scheme Y extends uniquely to a k-morphism X→Y, and rational maps X⇢Y are exactly such morphisms; the finite closed complement is handled by local DVRs and the valuative criterion.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
The Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes, §§29, 33-35, 43
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21

items.strategy: The complement of the dense open domain is closed of dimension below one, hence finite. At each missing closed point x the local ring O_{X,x} is a DVR because X is smooth over k and one-dimensional, and the valuative criterion for the proper morphism Y→Spec k lifts the generic-point morphism Spec k(X)→Y to Spec O_{X,x}→Y; these partial morphisms agree with phi on the common generic point and glue by locality of morphism-sheaf data on the open cover. Uniqueness is the dense-open agreement corollary; AC enters through the DVR, valuative and finite-complement suppliers.

items.title: Smooth proper curves, dominant morphisms and function fields
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. (1) For smooth proper geometrically integral curves $C$ and $D$ over a field $k$, the assignment $f\mapsto f^*$ is a bijection from the set of dominant $k$-morphisms $C\to D$ onto the set of injective $k$-algebra homomorphisms $k(D)\hookrightarrow k(C)$. (2) Let $k$ be a perfect field and let $K/k$ be a finitely generated field extension of transcendence degree one in which $k$ is relatively algebraically closed. Then there exists a smooth proper geometrically integral curve $C$ over $k$ together with a $k$-algebra isomorphism $\varphi:K\to k(C)$. If $(C,\varphi)$ and $(C',\varphi')$ are two such models, there is a unique $k$-isomorphism $\psi:C'\to C$ with $\varphi'=\psi^*\circ\varphi$. Equivalently, over perfect $k$ the category of smooth proper geometrically integral $k$-curves with dominant morphisms is contravariantly equivalent to the category of finitely generated transcendence-degree-one field extensions of $k$ in which $k$ is relatively algebraically closed, with $k$-embeddings as morphisms.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy), Chs. 6-8
Jiahui Gao and Shouwu Zhang, Lectures on Algebraic Geometry (December 14, 2019), Ch. 7
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21

items.strategy: Build a normal affine model from K, compactify it projectively, normalize, and verify dimension, smoothness, geometric integrality, and the morphism correspondence.

items.title: Birational smooth proper curves are isomorphic
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let C and D be smooth proper geometrically integral curves over k. Every birational rational map C⇢D is represented by an isomorphism C→D. In particular every dominant morphism of such curves which is birational in the sense of birational morphisms of integral finite-type schemes is an isomorphism.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy), Chs. 6-8

items.strategy: A birational rational map corresponds to a k-isomorphism of function fields. The bijection of the function-field equivalence produces a dominant morphism C→D inducing that isomorphism, and the inverse field isomorphism produces a morphism D→C; the composites are dominant morphisms inducing the identity on the function field, hence are the identity by the same injectivity/determination argument, so the morphism is an isomorphism and represents the given rational map by uniqueness of representatives.

items.title: Local rings of a smooth curve are discrete valuation rings
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let C be a smooth curve over a field k and let x in C be a closed point. Then the local ring O_{C,x} is a Noetherian regular local ring of dimension one, hence a discrete valuation ring whose maximal ideal is generated by a uniformizer t_x. Consequently every nonzero rational function f in k(C)^x has a well-defined order ord_x(f) in Z, and every nonzero element of O_{C,x} is a unit times a power of t_x.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21
The Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes, §§29, 33-35, 43

items.strategy: In an affine chart the point corresponds to a maximal ideal of a finite-type k-domain of dimension one; smoothness over k makes the local ring geometrically regular hence regular, and the local dimension formula together with dimension equal to transcendence degree makes it one-dimensional over the residue field. The published theorem that one-dimensional regular local rings are DVRs then applies, and the DVR normal form gives the order and the uniformizer statement. AC enters through that theorem and the dimension interfaces.

items.title: Divisors on a smooth proper curve
items.statement: Let C be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over k. A divisor on C is an arbitrary finite formal Z-linear combination of closed points; this definition itself has no Choice premise. For the structural normality and Weil-divisor identification, assume AC (which supplies the invoked DC): each closed-point local ring is a DVR, the generic local ring is the field k(C), and consequently C is normal with closed points exactly its codimension-one points. Under the same assumption the closed-point local rings are PIDs and UFDs, and the generic local ring is a UFD, so C is locally factorial; the Cartier interpretation is supplied by the separate curve-level comparison. Support, positive and negative parts, degree, effectivity, and comparison D>=D' use the stated coefficientwise conventions.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy), Chs. 6-8
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21

items.title: Cartier and Weil divisors agree on a smooth curve
items.statement: Assume AC together with the inherited DC used by the Cartier-to-Weil cycle suppliers. Let C be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over k. At each closed point, O_{C,x} is a DVR, hence a PID and UFD; at the generic point the local ring is the field k(C). Thus C is locally factorial. Every Weil divisor on C is Cartier, and the Cartier-to-Weil cycle map CaDiv(C)->Div(C) is an isomorphism compatible with principal divisors. The induced map CaDiv(C)/Prin_C(C)->Pic(C) is an isomorphism, hence Pic(C)≅Cl(C); every invertible sheaf is O_C(D) for a divisor D unique up to linear equivalence.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Divisors, §§31.14-31.30
The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy), Chs. 6-8

items.strategy: DVRs are PIDs and PIDs are UFDs, so every local ring is factorial and the locally-factorial isomorphism identifies Weil and Cartier divisor classes and computes Pic as the class group; the rational-section theorem supplies O_C(D) for every invertible sheaf. Injectivity of the cycle map is the locally-factorial part of that same theorem, and well-definedness of cycles is the normal-scheme Cartier-to-Weil theorem. AC is declared for the curve structure; DC is inherited exactly from the two Cartier-to-Weil suppliers, which assume it.

items.title: The space L(D)
items.statement: Assume AC for the local-order and Cartier/Weil routes below, with DC supplied as stated. For a divisor D=sum_x n_x[x] on a smooth proper geometrically integral curve C over k, define L(D)={f in k(C)^x : div(f)+D>=0} together with 0. Membership is coefficientwise, ord_x(f)+n_x>=0, so negative n_x require zeros and positive n_x permit poles; L(D) is a k-subspace. The canonical inclusion H^0(C,O_C(D)) into k(C) has image exactly L(D), via the local subsheaf O_C(D) subset K_C and the generic rational function.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21
William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy), Chs. 6-8

items.title: Effective divisors linearly equivalent to D are sections modulo scalars
items.statement: Assume AC, which supplies DC for the curve Cartier-to-Weil interface. For a divisor D on a smooth proper geometrically integral curve C, [f]↦div(f)+D gives a bijection from the nonzero elements of L(D) modulo k^× to the effective divisors linearly equivalent to D. Thus L(D)=0 exactly when no effective divisor is linearly equivalent to D.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Divisors, §§31.14-31.30
The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21

items.strategy: Read f as a rational section of O_C(D); the rational-section theorem assigns div(f)+D and a global section precisely when the divisor is effective, with the same classes under scalar multiples, and the global-section/effective-divisor lemma gives the converse direction from an effective representative back to a nonzero section.

items.title: Complete linear system
items.statement: Let C be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over k and D a divisor. The complete linear system |D| is the set of effective divisors linearly equivalent to D; its set definition is choice-free. Under AC, nonzero functions in L(D) modulo k^× maps bijectively to |D| by [f]↦div(f)+D, so |D| is the set of k-lines P(L(D)) and is empty exactly when L(D)=0. The current finite-dimensionality result makes this a projective space of lines under AC, and changing D within its linear equivalence class preserves the associated effective divisors.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21
William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy), Chs. 6-8

items.title: Base points and base-point-free linear systems
items.statement: Assume AC for the current local-order, Cartier/Weil, section-dictionary, and finite-dimensionality routes, with DC supplied from AC. For V⊆L(D), a closed point x is a base point exactly when every nonzero f∈V has ord_x(f)+n_x≥1, equivalently every divisor in P(V) contains x. V is base-point-free exactly when the evaluation map O_C^{dim V}→O_C(D) is surjective, equivalently O_C(D) is globally generated by V. The zero subspace makes every closed point vacuously a base point and is not base-point-free.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21

items.title: A base-point-free linear system defines a morphism to projective space
items.statement: Assume AC and its DC consequence for the current projective-space, finite-dimensionality, and Cartier/Weil routes. For a base-point-free V⊆L(D) of dimension r+1≥1, a basis defines a morphism C→P^r_k up to PGL_{r+1}(k), with O_C(D)≅φ_V^*O(1); scheme-theoretic hyperplane pullbacks, including the empty hyperplane for r=0, correspond with multiplicities to the divisors in P(V). Conversely, a morphism with an isomorphism φ^*O(1)≅O_C(D) gives the base-point-free span of pulled-back global sections, and recovers φ when that span has dimension r+1; this span is independent of the isomorphism. A closed point is a base point exactly when evaluation fails to be surjective on its stalk.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21
William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy), Chs. 6-8

items.strategy: Base-point-freeness of V is exactly surjectivity of the evaluation morphism of O_C(D), so the published generating-sections theorem produces the morphism to relative projective space with O_C(D) isomorphic to the pullback of O(1), and the published data-equivalence theorem gives the converse and the hyperplane correspondence; translate the global generation into the divisor language with the Cartier-Weil identification.

items.title: Functions on a proper curve
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let C be a proper geometrically connected and geometrically reduced curve over k, for instance a smooth proper curve. Then the canonical map k->H^0(C,O_C) is an isomorphism. More generally, for a proper integral curve over k the k-algebra H^0(C,O_C) is a finite field extension of k, it equals k whenever C is geometrically connected and geometrically reduced, and hence for every proper curve over k, which is geometrically integral by definition.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21

items.strategy: The proper scheme C is nonempty and its algebraic-closure fibre is connected and reduced, so the published global-functions corollary applies; the general statement is the global-functions finiteness theorem together with the flat base-change computation of H^0 over an algebraic closure, which shows that the constants become k-bar precisely when the fibre is connected.

items.title: Genus and arithmetic genus of a curve
items.statement: For a smooth proper geometrically connected curve C, g(C)=h^1(C,O_C)=1-chi(O_C). For any integral proper finite-type k-scheme X whose Noetherian underlying space has dimension one, define p_a(X)=1-chi(O_X)=h^1(X,O_X)-h^0(X,O_X)+1; coherence, proper cohomology finiteness, and dimension-one vanishing make these finite invariants, without requiring X to be geometrically integral or smooth. For smooth proper geometrically connected C, p_a(C)=g(C).

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy), Chs. 6-8
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21

items.title: Canonical bundle and canonical divisors
items.statement: For a smooth curve C over k, the raw canonical sheaf is ω_C=Ω^1_{C/k}, without a Choice premise; under AC it is invertible. Under AC, the order of a nonzero rational differential at a closed point is the DVR order of its coefficient in any local frame, independent of the frame and valid for inseparable residue extensions. Its finite-support divisor is effective exactly for regular differentials. On a smooth proper geometrically integral curve, all canonical divisors are linearly equivalent as Weil and Cartier divisors and ω_C≅O_C(K_C); AC supplies DC for the Cartier-to-Weil route.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21
Jiahui Gao and Shouwu Zhang, Lectures on Algebraic Geometry (December 14, 2019), Ch. 7

items.title: Divisors of rational differentials form one linear equivalence class
items.statement: Assume AC, which supplies DC for the Cartier-to-Weil cycle suppliers. For nonzero rational differentials ω and ω′ on a smooth proper geometrically integral curve, there is a unique f∈k(C)^× with ω′=fω and div(ω′)=div(ω)+div_W(f). Their Weil and Cartier divisors are therefore linearly equivalent, forming one canonical class, and ω_C≅O_C(K_C) for every canonical divisor.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
Jiahui Gao and Shouwu Zhang, Lectures on Algebraic Geometry (December 14, 2019), Ch. 7
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21

items.strategy: The sheaf of relative differentials is invertible, so two nonzero rational sections differ by a unique rational function; compare their orders at each closed point using an arbitrary local frame of the invertible sheaf to obtain div(omega')=div(omega)+div(f), including points with inseparable residue fields. The Cartier/divisor dictionary used for the sheaf identification remains an explicit supplier obligation.

items.title: Nonconstant morphisms of proper curves are finite and surjective
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let f:C->D be a nonconstant k-morphism of proper integral curves over k. Then f is surjective and finite; in particular f is dominant, the comorphism embeds k(D) into k(C), and [k(C):k(D)] is finite.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves, Lemma 53.2.4 (tag 0CCL)
The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
The Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes, §§29, 33-35, 43
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21

items.strategy: A proper source over k mapping to a separated target gives a proper morphism. Its closed irreducible non-point image is all of D. Stacks Algebraic Curves Lemma 53.2.4 (0CCL) makes the morphism finite because the source is proper of dimension one and its sole one-dimensional component has non-point image. On a finite affine chart, the finite algebra has finite-dimensional generic fibre, giving [k(C):k(D)]<infinity. AC is inherited from the curve closed-subset supplier used for surjectivity.

items.title: Degree of a nonconstant morphism of curves
items.statement: Assume Choice for the finiteness route. A nonconstant morphism f:C→D of smooth proper geometrically integral curves is finite and surjective; deg(f)=[k(C):k(D)] is positive. For every closed q∈D, the exact finite-flat fibre formula is Σ_{p∈f⁻¹(q)} e_p[κ(p):κ(q)]=deg(f). Degree one is equivalent to birationality and, for these curves, to being an isomorphism; degrees multiply in composites by the field-extension tower law.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy), Chs. 6-8
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21

items.title: Ramification index of a morphism of curves
items.statement: Let f:C→D be a nonconstant map of smooth proper geometrically integral curves and p a closed point over q. The index e_p=ord_p(f^*t_q)>0 is independent of the target uniformizer. Index one is ordinary scheme-theoretic unramifiedness exactly when κ(p)/κ(q) is also separable; the index definition is choice-free, while this comparison uses the stated Choice-dependent criteria.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21
William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy), Chs. 6-8

items.title: Local support and index bound for the different of a curve map
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let f:C->D be a finite surjective morphism of smooth proper geometrically integral curves over a field k, with finite separable function-field extension k(C)/k(D). For a closed point p of C, put q=f(p), let e_p be its ramification index, and set l_p=length_{O_{C,p}}(Omega_{C/D,p}). Then Omega_{C/D} is coherent and torsion with finite support, and l_p>=e_p-1 for every p. More precisely, l_p=0 if and only if e_p=1 and kappa(p)/kappa(q) is separable; l_p=e_p-1 if and only if kappa(p)/kappa(q) is separable and e_p is invertible in kappa(q) (equivalently, the extension of DVRs is tamely ramified). If the residue extension is inseparable or the positive residue characteristic divides e_p, then l_p>=e_p. Consequently Supp(Omega_{C/D})={p:e_p>1 or kappa(p)/kappa(q) is inseparable}; when k is perfect this is exactly {p:e_p>1}.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves, Lemma 53.12.4 (tag 0C1F)
references.locator: Local assertions (1)-(3). The lemma also assumes H^0(X,O_X)=H^0(Y,O_Y)=k for its genus identity; this proof uses only its local setup and reproves the local assertions.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Quasi-finite syntomic morphisms, Lemma 49.10.1 (tag 0BWE)
references.locator: For a locally quasi-finite, flat lci map, gives the equivalent syntomic condition and local relative global complete-intersection presentation with n variables and n equations.

references.title: The Stacks Project, A formula for the different, Lemma 49.12.2 (tag 0BWD)
references.locator: For a quasi-finite relative complete intersection B=A[x_1,...,x_n,1/h]/(f_1,...,f_n), the Koszul/diagonal computation gives the Noether different generated by det(partial f_i/partial x_j); no perfectness or monogenicity hypothesis.

references.title: The Stacks Project, A formula for the different, Lemma 49.12.3 (tag 0BWG)
references.locator: For a quasi-finite syntomic map, identifies the trace different with the Kähler different; the map here is finite flat lci, hence satisfies these hypotheses.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Discriminants, Lemma 49.12.6 (tag 0BWJ)
references.locator: S Noetherian, X and Y smooth of the same relative dimension n over S, and f:Y->X locally quasi-finite; then f is flat and the different is cut out by wedge^n(df). Applied with S=Spec(k), n=1; its proof computes the zeroth Fitting ideal from the cotangent sequence.

items.strategy: The generic differential module vanishes by separability and has finite support. At each closed point, completion splits the finite flat algebra into completed DVR factors and preserves lengths. For the local factor A→B, graph factorization gives lci; a square complete-intersection presentation gives Fitt_0(Omega)=(det J), and the diagonal Koszul calculation plus finite-free trace duality identifies this with the trace different (h), where Hom_A(B,A)=B lambda and tau=h lambda. The fibre trace functional is nonzero exactly when the residue extension is separable and e is invertible; then h mod s^e is a nonzero socle element and ord(h)=e−1. If it vanishes, h is divisible by s^e and ord(h)≥e.

items.title: Fibre degree sum with ramification and residue degrees
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let f:C->D be a nonconstant morphism of smooth proper geometrically integral curves over k, put n=deg(f), and let q be a closed point of D. Then the fibre f^{-1}(q) is finite and sum over p in f^{-1}(q) of e_p [kappa(p):kappa(q)] = n.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
Jiahui Gao and Shouwu Zhang, Lectures on Algebraic Geometry (December 14, 2019), Ch. 7
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21

items.strategy: Put A=O_{D,q} and B=H^0(Spec A,f_*O_C). Finiteness of f makes B a finite A-algebra, and B embeds into the function field k(C), so B is torsion-free over the DVR A, hence free of rank [k(C):k(D)]=n. At each maximal ideal of B the localisation is O_{C,p}; decomposing B along the idempotents of the finite k-algebra B/mB, which lift because the uniformizer lies in the Jacobson radical, expresses length_A(B)=n as the sum of length_A(O_{C,p}) over the points p of the fibre. Writing f^*t_q=u t_p^{e_p} and using length_A(O_{C,p})=e_p[kappa(p):kappa(q)] gives the formula. AC is inherited from the finiteness of f.

items.title: Ramification points, branch points and unramifiedness
items.statement: Assume AC for the current finite-map, local-DVR, finite-presentation, and flatness interfaces. The index-ramification locus consists of closed points p with e_p>1; independently, the differential-ramification locus is Supp(Ω_{C/D}), and f is unramified (equivalently étale) at p exactly when Ω_{C/D,p}=0. For a separable function-field extension, the differential support is finite and consists of closed points with e_p>1 or inseparable residue extension. The two loci agree at separable-residue points, everywhere over a perfect field, and can differ over an imperfect field; no comparison is asserted for an inseparable function-field extension.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21
Jiahui Gao and Shouwu Zhang, Lectures on Algebraic Geometry (December 14, 2019), Ch. 7

items.title: The different divisor of a generically separable morphism
items.statement: Assume AC and let f:C→D be a finite surjective morphism of smooth proper geometrically integral curves with separable function-field extension. For each closed p, set l_p=length_{O_{C,p}}(Ω_{C/D,p}); the current local-different result makes these nonnegative integers with finite support, l_p≥e_p−1, and l_p=0 exactly when e_p=1 and κ(p)/κ(f(p)) is separable. The effective different divisor R_f=Σ_p l_p[p] has differential-ramification support. Its support agrees with the index-ramification locus over perfect k and may additionally contain inseparable-residue points over an imperfect field.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21
Jiahui Gao and Shouwu Zhang, Lectures on Algebraic Geometry (December 14, 2019), Ch. 7

items.title: An invertible quotient of an invertible subsheaf by a torsion sheaf is a twist by an effective divisor
items.statement: Assume Choice. For any field k and smooth proper geometrically integral curve C, an inclusion of invertible sheaves with torsion quotient of finite closed-point lengths l_p gives M≅L⊗O_C(D), where D=Σ l_p[p] is effective; the quotient M/L is generally noncanonically isomorphic to O_C(D)/O_C.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Divisors, §§31.14-31.30
The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21

items.strategy: Apply the rational-section dictionary to the invertible sheaf M⊗L^{-1} and its canonical rational section. At a closed point p the DVR local ring makes both sheaves free of rank one, so L_p=(t_p^{l_p}) inside M_p=O_{C,p}, the section has order l_p>=0, and the resulting Cartier divisor is effective with multiplicity l_p at p; the identity M≅L⊗O_C(D) follows from the Cartier-Weil dictionary and the local length computation.

items.title: Canonical bundle formula with the different
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice where the coherence and differential suppliers require it. Let f:C->D be a finite surjective morphism of smooth proper geometrically integral curves over k with separable function-field extension k(C)/k(D). Then the natural map f^*omega_D->omega_C induced by differentiation is injective with cokernel Omega_{C/D}, and there is a canonical isomorphism omega_C≅f^*omega_D⊗O_C(R_f), equivalently K_C is linearly equivalent to f^*K_D+R_f for canonical divisors, where R_f is the different divisor of f.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
Jiahui Gao and Shouwu Zhang, Lectures on Algebraic Geometry (December 14, 2019), Ch. 7
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21

items.strategy: The transitivity sequence f^*Omega_D->Omega_C->Omega_{C/D}->0 is exact by the affine-local transitivity lemma and base-change compatibility. Separability makes Omega_{C/D} vanish at the generic point, because the finite separable field extension has zero differentials; the kernel of f^*omega_D->omega_C is then a subsheaf of the invertible omega_C vanishing generically, hence zero, so the map is injective, and the cokernel is the torsion module Omega_{C/D} of the different. The torsion-quotient lemma identifies omega_C with f^*omega_D twisted by the effective divisor of the lengths l_p, which is R_f.

items.title: Effective divisors have nonnegative degree
items.statement: Let C be a proper geometrically integral curve over a field k and let D=sum_x n_x[x] be an effective divisor. Then deg_k(D)=sum_x n_x[kappa(x):k] is a nonnegative integer, and deg_k(D)=0 if and only if D=0: residue fields of closed points are finite extensions of k, so each degree [kappa(x):k] is positive.

references.title: William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy), Chs. 6-8
The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)

items.strategy: All coefficients are nonnegative and every residue field of a closed point is a finite extension of k, hence of degree at least one; the only vanishing effective divisor is the empty sum.

items.title: Negative-degree line bundles have no nonzero sections
items.statement: Assume AC and its DC consequence for the Cartier-to-Weil interface. If L is an invertible sheaf on a smooth proper geometrically integral curve and its degree is represented by deg_k(D) for L≅O_C(D), then deg(L)<0 implies H^0(C,L)=0. In particular, a line bundle with a nonzero global section has nonnegative degree.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy), Chs. 6-8

items.strategy: A nonzero section of L=O_C(D) gives an effective divisor linearly equivalent to D, by the sections-modulo-scalars lemma; effective divisors have nonnegative degree and degree is invariant under linear equivalence by the degree homomorphism on Pic, so deg(L)>=0. AC enters through that degree homomorphism.

items.title: A nonconstant rational function defines a finite map to the projective line
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let C be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over k and let f in k(C)^x be nonconstant. Then f defines a finite locally free morphism phi_f:C->P^1_k of degree [k(C):k(f)], whose fibre over infinity is the pole divisor (f)_infinity=sum_{ord_x(f)<0}(-ord_x(f))[x] of degree [k(C):k(f)], and whose fibre over zero is the zero divisor; a rational function with no poles is algebraic over k and is a global unit.

references.title: William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy), Chs. 6-8
The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21

items.strategy: A smooth curve is normal, so the in-run normal-curve rational-function-map lemma produces the finite locally free morphism with affine coordinate f; its fibre-degree computation identifies the zero and infinity fibres with the divisor of f, giving the pole divisor and its degree. The algebraic case is the global-unit clause of that lemma.

items.title: Gonality
items.statement: The gonality of a smooth proper geometrically integral curve C over k is the minimum degree of a nonconstant k-morphism C→P^1_k. Under AC the degree set is nonempty by the current rational-function finite-map route, and the minimum exists as a positive integer. Under AC, gon(C)=1 exactly when C≅P^1_k.

references.title: William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy), Chs. 6-8
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21

items.title: Geometric genus of a singular curve
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $k$ be a perfect field ([[def-perfect-field]]). Let $X$ be a curve over $k$ ([[def-algebraic-curve-over-field]]) that is proper over $k$. Write $
u:X^{\mathrm{nu}}	o X$ for its normalization from [[thm-normalization-glues-integral-finite-type-curves]]. We first verify that this normalization is itself a proper geometrically integral curve of chain dimension one, and then verify its smoothness before using the curve-genus definition. First, $X$ is integral, separated, finite type, and has chain dimension one because it is a curve. Choose a finite affine cover $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ of $X$. Since $
u$ is finite, $
u^{-1}(U_i)=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ and $B_i$ is module-finite over $A_i$ ([[def-finite-morphism-schemes]], [[lem-finite-morphism-affine]]). Each $A_i$ is a finite-type $k$-domain, so a finite set of algebra generators for $A_i$ together with a finite $A_i$-module generating set for $B_i$ generates $B_i$ as a $k$-algebra ([[def-finite-type-and-module-finite-algebras]]). Thus $X^{\mathrm{nu}}$ is finite type over $k$. Its chain dimension is one as well. The chain-dimension hypothesis on $X$ gives a strict chain $Z_0\subsetneq Z_1$ of nonempty irreducible closed subsets. Since $X$ is irreducible, $Z_1=X$: otherwise adjoining $X$ would give a chain of length two. Choose a point of $Z_0$ and an affine neighborhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of it. The nonempty open $U$ contains the generic point of $X$, so $Z_0\cap U$ is a nonempty proper irreducible closed subset of $U$. No chain in $U$ can have length two: if two closed subsets of $U$ had equal closures in $X$, intersecting the common closure with $U$ would make the original subsets equal ([[thm-subspace-closure-and-interior]]). The chain $Z_0\cap U\subsetneq U$ therefore shows that $U$ has dimension one. Closed irreducible subsets $V(\mathfrak p)$ of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ correspond in reverse order to prime ideals ([[def-prime-spectrum-and-vanishing-sets]]), so this is the ring dimension used in [[thm-affine-domain-dimension-transcendence-degree]]. Since $\operatorname{Frac}(A)=k(X)$, that theorem gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_k k(X)=1$. Every nonempty affine chart $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $X^{\mathrm{nu}}$ is a finite-type domain with $\operatorname{Frac}(B)=k(X)$ by the normalization theorem and the function field lemma [[lem-integral-finite-type-scheme-function-field]]. Hence $\dim B=1$. To compare with chain dimension, any chain of irreducible closed subsets of $X^{\mathrm{nu}}$ can be restricted to an affine neighborhood meeting its smallest member. Each trace is a nonempty irreducible closed subset of that affine open. Strictness is preserved: for nested irreducible closed subsets $Z\subsetneq Z'$, both the chosen affine neighborhood's intersection with $Z'$ and $Z'\setminus Z$ are nonempty open subsets of the irreducible space $Z'$, so they intersect ([[lem-irreducibility-criteria-and-open-subspaces]]). Conversely, a strict chain of closed subsets in an affine open remains strict after taking closures in the whole scheme, by [[thm-subspace-closure-and-interior]]. Thus the affine-chart dimensions give chain dimension one for $X^{\mathrm{nu}}$. The map $
u$ is finite, hence proper ([[cor-finite-morphism-proper]]); composing it with the proper structure map $X	o\operatorname{Spec}k$ shows that $X^{\mathrm{nu}}$ is proper ([[lem-composite-finite-proper-morphism-proper]]). In particular its structure map is separated, since proper means separated, finite type and universally closed ([[def-proper-morphism]]). It remains to check geometric integrality. Fix an algebraic closure $ ar k$ of $k$, and put $K=k(X)=k(X^{\mathrm{nu}})$. Since $X$ is geometrically integral, [[lem-integral-finite-type-scheme-function-field]] gives that $K\otimes_k ar k$ is a domain (under the stated Choice premise). For each nonempty affine chart $V_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ of $X^{\mathrm{nu}}$, the function-field identification embeds $B_i$ into $K$. The $k$-module $ ar k$ is flat by [[prop-modules-over-a-field-are-projective-flat-and-injective]], so tensoring this injection gives $B_i\otimes_k ar k\hookrightarrow K\otimes_k ar k$. Thus each chart ring $B_i\otimes_k ar k$ is a nonzero domain. For any pair of these charts their intersection is nonempty because it contains the generic point; it is affine because $X^{\mathrm{nu}}$ is separated, by [[thm-separatedness-gluing-overlap-criterion]]. Write it as $W_{ij}=\operatorname{Spec}D_{ij}$. The same function-field identification embeds $D_{ij}$ into $K$, so flatness gives $D_{ij}\otimes_k ar k\hookrightarrow K\otimes_k ar k$. This is a nonzero domain. By [[lem-base-extension-field-coordinate-ring]], these tensor-product charts and overlaps are exactly the charts and intersections after extension to $ ar k$. Nonzero affine rings have points under Choice, by [[thm-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal-ideal]], so the base-changed charts cover a nonempty scheme and remain pairwise intersecting. A cover by integral affine opens with pairwise nonempty intersections is reduced and irreducible; therefore $X^{\mathrm{nu}}_{ ar k}$ is integral. This proves geometric integrality by [[def-geometric-fibre]] and [[def-geometrically-reduced-integral-connected-fibre]]. We have now established that $X^{\mathrm{nu}}$ is a proper geometrically integral separated finite-type curve of chain dimension one. Its finite affine cover above has Noetherian coordinate rings by the finite-type-over-a-field case of [[cor-finite-type-algebra-over-a-principal-ideal-domain-is-noetherian]], so $X^{\mathrm{nu}}$ is Noetherian by [[def-locally-noetherian-and-noetherian-scheme]]. Its normality means that its local rings are integrally closed domains ([[def-weil-divisor-normal-noetherian-scheme]]). The localizations of the chart rings are Noetherian by [[thm-noetherian-ring-quotients-and-localisations]]. At a non-generic point $x$, an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}B$ identifies $x$ with a nonzero prime $\mathfrak p$. The chain $0\subsetneq\mathfrak p$ and the dimension-one bound give $\dim B_{\mathfrak p}=1$. Thus $\mathcal O_{X^{\mathrm{nu}},x}$ is a one-dimensional Noetherian local integrally closed domain, hence a discrete valuation ring by [[thm-equivalent-characterisations-of-a-dvr]] and therefore regular. The generic local ring is the field $K$, also regular. So $X^{\mathrm{nu}}$ is regular; since $k$ is perfect, it is smooth by [[thm-regular-equals-smooth-over-perfect-field]]. The **geometric genus** of $X$ is $$ g(X):=g(X^{\mathrm{nu}})=h^1(X^{\mathrm{nu}},\mathcal O_{X^{\mathrm{nu}}}), $$ the genus [[def-arithmetic-genus-proper-curve]] of the smooth proper curve $X^{\mathrm{nu}}$. It is a nonnegative integer, finite-dimensionality of the cohomology being part of that definition. If $X$ is itself smooth, then $X$ is regular by [[thm-regular-equals-smooth-over-perfect-field]] and therefore normal ([[thm-regular-local-rings-are-normal]]). The normalization's initiality then identifies $
u$ with an isomorphism, so $g(X)$ is the genus of $X$. The definition is independent of all choices: the normalization is unique up to unique isomorphism over $X$ ([[thm-normalization-glues-integral-finite-type-curves]]), and the genus of a smooth proper curve is an isomorphism invariant of the curve together with its structure morphism to $k$. We do not call $g(X)$ the genus of $X$ without qualification, reserving the unqualified word for the smooth case; the geometric genus is an invariant of the singular curve $X$ and is insensitive to the singularities, in contrast with the arithmetic genus $p_a(X)=1-\chi(\mathcal O_X)$.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy), Chs. 6-8
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21

items.title: Delta invariant of a curve singularity
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice and let X be an integral proper finite-type curve over any algebraically closed field k, with normalization ν:Xⁿᵘ→X. For a closed point x, δₓ(X)=dimₖ((ν₊O_{Xⁿᵘ})ₓ/O_{X,x}); each local invariant is a finite nonnegative integer and vanishes exactly at regular points. The singular locus is finite, so the total delta invariant is a finite sum in every characteristic. Choice is inherited from the cited normalization, coherence, regular-local, regular-locus and curve-topology interfaces.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy), Chs. 6-8
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21

items.title: Arithmetic genus, geometric genus and delta invariants
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice and let k be algebraically closed. Let X be an integral proper finite-type curve over k with normalization nu:X^nu->X. Then p_a(X)=g(X^nu)+sum_{x in X} delta_x, the sum being finite and supported on the singular points of X; equivalently g(X^nu)=p_a(X)-sum_x delta_x.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy), Chs. 6-8
Jiahui Gao and Shouwu Zhang, Lectures on Algebraic Geometry (December 14, 2019), Ch. 7

items.strategy: Use the normalization exact sequence and Euler-characteristic additivity as before. For the cokernel Q, define its annihilator sheaf; prove on affine charts that annihilators localize using a finite set of generators. The quasi-coherent annihilator defines a closed subscheme with underlying support Supp(Q), retaining its nilpotents. Since Q is annihilated by that ideal, descend it canonically as a quasi-coherent module on the thickening. Decompose the finite underlying space into one-point open-and-closed affine components, identify the module of sections on each component with Q_x by the associated-sheaf stalk formula, and apply closed-immersion cohomology, finite-disjoint-union cohomology, and affine vanishing to obtain chi(Q)=sum_x delta_x. Preserve the stated genus identity.

items.title: Arithmetic genus of a plane curve
items.statement: Assume AC. For a homogeneous form F of degree d≥1 over a field k, if X=V_+(F)⊂P²_k is integral and one-dimensional (without a geometric-integrality or smoothness hypothesis), then H⁰(X,O_X)=k, H¹(X,O_X)≅k[T₀,T₁,T₂]_{d−3}, and p_a(X)=1−χ(O_X)=(d−1)(d−2)/2; the polynomial piece is zero for d≤2.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy), Chs. 6-8
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21

items.strategy: The structure sequence 0->O_{P^2}(-d)->O_{P^2}->i_*O_X->0 of the hypersurface supplier, together with the published cohomology of twists on P^2, kills the higher cohomology except in degree two, where the boundary identifies H^1(X,O_X) with the degree d-3 part of the polynomial ring of dimension (d-1)(d-2)/2; the long exact sequence also gives H^0(X,O_X)=k. Then p_a=1-chi is the alternating sum of the computed dimensions.

items.title: Geometric genus of a plane curve by delta invariants
items.statement: Let k be algebraically closed and let F in k[T0,T1,T2] be irreducible homogeneous of degree d>=1 defining an integral plane curve X=V_+(F) whose singularities are isolated. Then the genus of the normalization is g(X^nu)=(d-1)(d-2)/2 - sum_{x in X} delta_x, the sum over the finitely many singular points of X.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy), Chs. 6-8
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21

items.strategy: Combine the plane arithmetic-genus computation with the normalization formula p_a(X)=g(X^nu)+sum delta_x and rewrite g(X^nu) as the geometric genus; isolated singularities are automatic for an integral curve of dimension one and the sum is finite.

items.title: Composite of a finite morphism and a proper morphism is proper
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, used through the valuative criterion for proper
morphisms and the universal closedness of finite morphisms. Let $h:X\to Y$ be
a finite morphism of schemes and let $g:Y\to S$ be a proper morphism. Then the
composite $g\circ h:X\to S$ is proper. The same argument gives that a
composite of a finite morphism with a separated morphism is separated, and a
composite of finite-type morphisms is finite type; these two auxiliary facts
are proved as steps below because the composite is not assumed separated in
advance.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes, §§29, 33-35, 43
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21

items.title: Projective-line curve and divisor basics

references.title: The Stacks Project; elementary local prerequisite for the Step 5b citation repair

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For every field $k$, $\mathbb P^1_k$ is a smooth proper geometrically integral curve of genus zero. Write $t=x_1/x_0$ and $\infty=[0:1]$. Every closed point in the $t$-chart is $p=V(g)$ for a monic irreducible $g\in k[t]$; if $d=\deg g$, then $[\kappa(p):k]=d$ and $\operatorname{div}(g)=[p]-d[\infty]$. Every divisor $D$ is linearly equivalent to $\deg_k(D)[\infty]$, and $\mathcal O(1)\cong\mathcal O(\infty)$.
items.strategy: Direct elementary proof in the item; all supplier hypotheses and Choice uses are explicit.

items.title: The projective-line twisting sheaf is ample

references.title: The Stacks Project; elementary local prerequisite for the Step 5b citation repair

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. The sheaf $\mathcal O(1)$ on $\mathbb P^1_k$ is ample for every field $k$.
items.strategy: Direct elementary proof in the item; all supplier hypotheses and Choice uses are explicit.

items.title: Cohomology of a two-chart double cover

references.title: The Stacks Project; elementary local prerequisite for the Step 5b citation repair

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be a field, let $g$ be a nonnegative integer, fix polynomials $f\in k[x]$ and $\psi\in k[t]$, and let $C$ be a separated $k$-scheme with an affine open cover $U,V$, where $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_C)=k[x,y]/(y^2-f(x))$ and $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_C)=k[t,w]/(w^2-\psi(t))$. Suppose that $U\cap V=D_U(x)=D_V(t)$ and the gluing sends $t=x^{-1}$ and $w=x^{-(g+1)}y$. Then $H^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$ has dimension $g$ over $k$, with basis given by the classes of $x^{-1}y,\ldots,x^{-g}y$ (an empty basis when $g=0$).
items.strategy: Direct elementary proof in the item; all supplier hypotheses and Choice uses are explicit.

title: Smooth Proper Curves Divisors Genus and Ramification — Examples

items.title: Divisors and complete linear systems on the projective line
items.statement: On P^1_k, div(p)=Z(p)-m[∞] for a nonzero polynomial of degree m; deg(d[∞])=d; L(d[∞]) has dimension d+1 for d≥0 and is zero for d<0. For d≥0, |d[∞]| is the set of effective divisors of degree d, identified with k-lines in L(d[∞]) or k-rational points of its projective scheme of lines. The associated map is the degree-d Veronese closed immersion for d≥1; for d=0 it is the constant map P^1→P^0, and for d<0 there is no associated projective morphism.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy), Chs. 6-8
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21

items.title: A smooth conic is a projective line once it has a rational point
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a field k of characteristic not two, a smooth conic C in P^2 with a k-rational point p is isomorphic to P^1 by projection from p and residual intersection. For every k-rational point P of C, dim_k L([P])=2; p_a(C)=0 and C agrees with its normalization.

references.title: William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy), Chs. 6-8
The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)

items.title: Ramification of the double cover y^2=f(x)
items.statement: Assume k is algebraically closed of characteristic not 2 and f∈k[x] is squarefree of degree n=2g+1 or 2g+2, g≥1. The smooth projective model C of y²=f(x) maps to P^1 by a degree-two cover branched at the roots of f and also infinity when n is odd. Its plane model has degree n and p_a=(n−1)(n−2)/2; infinity is its only possible singular point and is singular exactly for n≥4, with δ∞=(n−1)(n−2)/2−g. For n=3,g=1 the plane cubic is smooth and δ∞=0. In all cases g(C)=g.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21
William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy), Chs. 6-8

items.strategy: Use the squarefree double-cover charts for smoothness and ramification; compute H1 directly as a two-open Cech quotient with basis x^-1 y,...,x^-g y. Establish projectivity by finite pullback of the ample O(1) and then ample powers. Compute delta from the plane genus correction.

items.title: The separability hypothesis in the ramification formula is necessary
items.statement: Assume Choice wherever the cited suppliers require it. In characteristic p>0 the p-th-power map P¹→P¹ has degree p and e₀=e∞=p; after algebraic closure every geometric closed point has index p, while over an imperfect field a closed point can have index 1 with purely inseparable residue extension. The relative differentials are invertible with zero torsion, so the proposed torsion-submodule extension of the canonical-bundle formula fails; this does not assign the separable different divisor to an inseparable map.

references.title: Jiahui Gao and Shouwu Zhang, Lectures on Algebraic Geometry (December 14, 2019), Ch. 7
The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21

items.title: Nodal cubic: arithmetic genus one, delta one, geometric genus zero
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let k be algebraically closed with char(k) != 2 and X=V_+(Y^2Z-X^3-X^2Z) with node o=(0:0:1). Then p_a(X)=1, o is the unique ordinary node with delta_o(X)=1, and the normalization is P^1 with geometric genus 0, via (T:S) -> (S(T^2-S^2):T(T^2-S^2):S^3).

references.title: William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy), Chs. 6-8
The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21

items.title: Cuspidal cubic: delta invariant and normalization
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let k be algebraically closed with char(k) != 2,3 and X=V_+(Y^2Z-X^3) with cusp o=(0:0:1). Then p_a(X)=1, o is the unique cusp with delta_o(X)=1, and the normalization is P^1 via t -> (t^2:t^3:1), of geometric genus 0.

references.title: William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy), Chs. 6-8
The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21

items.title: Smoothness of the source cannot be dropped in the extension of rational maps
items.statement: In characteristic not 2, the integral nodal curve y²=x²(x+1) remains integral over every field extension; its smooth locus is exactly D(x), while the node has embedding dimension two and local dimension one. The slope map y/x on D(x) does not extend to the curve because the two normalization points t=±1 above the node force different target values. If an extension exists for a reduced source and separated target, it is unique.

references.title: William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy), Chs. 6-8
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21

items.title: Divisor degree with residue degrees over a nonclosed field
items.statement: Assume Choice as inherited from the degree homomorphism. On P¹_ℝ, x=V(t²+1) has residue degree two, so D=[x] has degree two despite having one-point support; div(t²+1)=[x]−2[∞]. After base change to ℂ, x splits into two degree-one points and the total degree remains two.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21
William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy), Chs. 6-8

items.title: A linear system with and without a base point
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. On P^1 with D=2[infinity], V=span(1,t^2) is base-point-free and defines t -> t^2; W=span(t,t^2) has the unique base point 0, while its rational map [t:t^2]=[1:t] extends to the identity although the pair does not generate O(D) at 0. For char(k) != 2, P(W) is tangent to b^2=4ac and P(V) is a secant. In char(k)=2 the discriminant is the double line b^2=0, P(V) is its reduced support, and P(W) meets the double discriminant in a length-two point; the coordinate-square parametrization is geometrically onto the support but need not be onto k-points over an imperfect field.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21

items.title: A nontrivial degree-zero line bundle has no nonzero section
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the degree and Cartier-Weil suppliers. Let k be algebraically closed and let E be a smooth plane cubic y^2 z=x^3+axz^2+bz^3, a curve of genus one, with distinct closed points P and Q. Then L=O_E(P-Q) is a nontrivial invertible sheaf of degree zero with H^0(E,L)=0: a nonzero section would present L as O_E(D) with D effective and deg D=0, forcing D=0 and L trivial, while nontriviality holds because O_E(P-Q)≅O_E would give a rational function with divisor P-Q and hence a degree-one map E->P^1, impossible for a genus-one curve. This shows that degree zero neither forces triviality nor produces sections.

references.title: William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy), Chs. 6-8
The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21

items.title: Ramification indices of the power map on the projective line
items.statement: Let k be a field of characteristic not dividing n and let phi:P^1_k->P^1_k, [s:t]|->[s^n:t^n]. Then phi is finite of degree n, unramified away from 0 and infinity, and totally ramified at 0 and at infinity with e=n: the pullback of a uniformizer at the image point has order exactly n, and the fibre degree sum reads n=n at each of the two branch points. In the tame case the ramification divisor has support {0,infinity} with lengths n-1 at each point.

references.title: Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21

items.title: Smooth plane quartic has genus three
items.statement: Over algebraically closed k, a smooth plane quartic is geometrically integral: a repeated factor or a positive-degree factorization would produce a singular point by the Jacobian criterion and Bezout. It has p_a=3, all delta invariants vanish, and hence geometric genus 3, the degree-four case of the triangular-number genus formula.
